_provenance.experiment: Matched-initialization control for the crowd-sourced annotation (marginalized Dawid-Skene) benchmark
_provenance.hypothesis: Under the standard PPLBench protocol the three baselines (NumPyro/Stan/Turing) collapse to trials-as-chains ESS medians ~8 not because their NUTS kernels are slow, but because their default random init lets exactly one of four trials land in an inferior label-permutation mode (per-trial PLL ~-1850 vs the -1805..-1810 dominant band), which craters the pooled ESS. Impulse initializes deterministically at the uniform-simplex point (unconstrained z=0) and all its trials land in the dominant mode. Prediction: giving the baselines the SAME deterministic init removes the ~-1850 trials, recovers baseline ESS medians to thousands, and shrinks the n_eff/s gap vs Impulse to roughly the per-trial wall-time ratios (~2.2x / ~24x / ~56x).
_provenance.verdict: CONFIRMED. With matched init, every baseline trial lands in the dominant mode (no PLL ~-1850 outlier remains). ESS medians recover from ~8 to ~18600-19000 (2000x-2300x). The residual Impulse/baseline n_eff/s gap collapses to the per-trial wall-time ratio: NumPyro 2.10x (wall 2.30x), Stan 23.2x (wall 24.9x), Turing 58.1x (wall 62x). This isolates the baseline collapse as an initialization-policy artifact, not a kernel-speed difference; Impulse's remaining advantage is exactly its per-iteration wall-clock (compiler) speed.

init_point.description: Deterministic uniform-simplex point, identical for every trial and every system; equals Impulse's NUTS start.

constrained.confusion_matrix: every one of k*K=30 rows = ones(K)/K = [1/3, 1/3, 1/3]  (k=10 labelers, K=3)

init_point.unconstrained: z = 0 (62-dim: (K-1) + k*K*(K-1) = 2 + 60). Under the centered stick-breaking transform the uniform simplex is exactly the unconstrained origin, i.e. the symmetric point.
init_point.impulse_evidence: standard/crowd_sourced_annotation.jl build_constraint L111-119: init_prev = fill(1/K, K); init_conf = fill(1/K, k, K, K); fed as the constraint to ProbProg.generate in nuts_program (harness.jl L37) so the NUTS chain starts from that trace.

mechanism_per_system.numpyro: impl.matched_init_params(data) returns the constrained uniform dict; numpyro_harness.py converts it to unconstrained z via numpyro.infer.init_to_value (constrained_to_unconstrained) and passes init_params=z to mcmc.run for ALL trials (fixed across trials). The constrained sizes are NOT used to set inverse_mass_matrix (guarded), so the kernel is otherwise identical to the standard protocol. Verified: unconstrained z dim=62, max|z|=1.11e-16 (== symmetric point).
mechanism_per_system.stan: impl.matched_init_params(data) returns the constrained uniform dict; stan_harness.py passes it as CmdStan `inits` (Stan inits are constrained) for every trial. Verified: Stan accepted the simplex init (no rejection); init printed.
mechanism_per_system.turing: matched_init_params(data) returns NamedTuple (prev=fill(1/K,K), conf=fill(1/K,K,k*K)); turing_harness.jl passes it via DynamicPPL.InitFromParams (constrained, typed_identity) as sample()'s initial_params for every trial. Verified: logjoint at matched-init point finite (-3399.0 at k=10); init printed.

_provenance.config: pplbench_configs/standard/crowd_sourced_annotation_matched_init.json (identical model block/seed 12345/iterations 4000/warmup 1000/trials 4 to the standard config; impulse arms omitted; matched_init:true added to the numpyro/stan/turing infer_args).

matched_init.numpyro_superseded_buggy_first_run: outputs/2026-07-14_16:06:26 (matched init reached only trial 0; server-loop fell back to default init for trials 1-3; superseded by 16:08:21 after fix)

protocol.ess_metric: arviz pooled ESS over the 4 trials-as-chains (post-warmup); median over all latent scalar params.

notes: Impulse is the default-protocol reference (already deterministic uniform init); it was NOT re-run.

Baseline per-trial wall times are essentially unchanged vs default init (same kernel): NumPyro 8.33->8.53s, Stan 91.96->92.37s; Turing 212.3->231.0s (a ~9% increase driven by one 247s trial; trials 0-2 were 212-228s, in line with default).

The generic SVI helper _svi_init_constrained is buggy for this model (applies stick-breaking to zeros(K), yielding a length-(K+1)=4 'simplex' at 1/4 rather than the K=3 uniform simplex), so it was NOT reused; the matched init is built directly as the constrained uniform point per system.
